title: Stellar Insurance - Procurement MSA/DPA SLA Review
summary: Procurement-led review of Redwood MSA/DPA and proposed SLAs. Customer requested clarifications on data residency, KMS/HSM integration, breach notification timelines, and commercial approval path. Redwood AE/SE walked through proposed redlines, SLA tiers, and onboarding milestones. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA, security pack, and pricing deck; customer to review with InfoSec and Legal and revert by next week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Jordan Price (Stellar Procurement), Dr. Anika Patel (Stellar InfoSec), Samir Gupta (Stellar Legal), Riley Okoye (Stellar Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, uh I think we have Luis from our SE team with me. Um Jordan, thanks for coordinating on the procurement side.
[00:12] Jordan Price: Yep, thanks Maya. Quick note, we have Samir and Anika and Riley from our side. We want to go through MSA and DPA redlines and double check the SLA language because our finance needs the pricing approval by next Tuesday.
[00:25] Luis Ortega: Great, I'll be prepared to dive into the SLA/ops details, latency and also private deployment options.
[00:32] Dr. Anika Patel: Hi. Our primary concerns: data residency for PII, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and breach notification timelines. Also SOC 2 scope.
[00:42] Samir Gupta: From legal, main ask is a 60-day cure period, limits on liability, and standard indemnities. We'll flag a couple clauses in the MSA.
[00:51] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) walk MSA redlines, 2) DPA items, 3) SLA tiers and measurement, 4) pricing and procurement next steps, 5) onboarding timeline. Sound good?
[01:00] Jordan Price: Yep.

[01:22] Maya Chen: OK jumping in. On the MSA we saw your redline on the liability cap. Our standard is 12 months of fees or $1M whichever is higher. You requested a lower cap and carve-outs for gross negligence. We can be flexible on carve-outs but the cap is tied to our underwriting.
[01:40] Samir Gupta: Right, underwriting is fine but we can't expose Stellar to unlimited risk. Can we get a middle ground? 6 months of fees?
[01:49] Luis Ortega: Just to add, the Dedicated product has different pricing/commitment so cap calculations change if you go dedicated (reserved capacity) we can discuss different terms.
[02:02] Riley Okoye: Curious on SLA. Our apps need 99.95% availability for inference endpoints during business hours. What SLA tier maps to that?
[02:11] Luis Ortega: Our enterprise SLA 99.95% (annual) is available on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has 99.9% by default. For latency SLOs we provide p50/p95 numbers per model and route in the console.
[02:27] Dr. Anika Patel: And where do logs and audit trails live? We need audit logs retained for 3 years for compliance.
[02:35] Maya Chen: We provide audit logs, can retain up to 1 year on hosted by default; extended retention is available as an add-on  we can include a 3-year retention add-on for enterprise customers. For Private you can manage retention in your environment.

[03:02] Jordan Price: On the DPA, question on data classification: are embeddings or inference outputs considered customer data under your DPA?
[03:12] Luis Ortega: Yes, outputs and embeddings tied to customer requests are treated as customer data. We can scope the DPA to explicitly call that out.
[03:21] Samir Gupta: Also we need stronger deletion language  30 days after contract termination for hosted, and confirmation in writing.
[03:31] Maya Chen: We can agree to 30 days for hosted, with a certified deletion report. For private deployments, you retain control.

[03:58] Dr. Anika Patel: KMS: we need to use our HSM-backed keys and rotate keys quarterly. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM integration?
[04:08] Luis Ortega: Yes  we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and bring-your-own-key for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer keys in KMS. Quarterly rotation is supported but we should run a short technical runbook.
[04:25] Riley Okoye: Will that require service downtime during rotation?
[04:30] Luis Ortega: No, key rotation is seamless with envelope keys; there are steps for cache invalidation for long-running KV caches, but no planned downtime. We'll share the runbook.

[04:58] Maya Chen: On breach notification: you asked for 24 hours. Our standard is 72 hours for security incidents. Can you explain why 24?
[05:09] Dr. Anika Patel: Regulatorily, our BAAs/insurers expect 24 hours for incidents impacting PII.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Understood. We can escalate to security leadership to see if 48 hours is an option but 24 is challenging across our customer base. We'll bring that back.

[05:44] Jordan Price: Pricing  we need a clear proposal that meeting our procurement thresholds. We're looking at a 12-month committed Dedicated plan for inference across multiple models. Need monthly spend forecast for approval.
[05:58] Maya Chen: We'll include a pricing deck with committed spend tiers, overage rules, and an estimate of unit economics. Also include a model of p50/p95 token usage.
[06:08] Samir Gupta: Any termination for convenience? We prefer a 30-day termination right after initial term, with prorated refunds.
[06:16] Maya Chen: Commercially we can look at shorter notice periods for later years, but initial committed term for Dedicated is usually 12 months with early termination fees tied to remaining committed value. We can propose a phased ramp to reduce risk.

[06:45] Luis Ortega: From a technical POV, onboarding timeline: pilot (2 weeks) -> performance benchmark (1 week) -> production cutover (2-4 weeks). For Dedicated there is provisioning time for reserved capacity typically 2-3 weeks depending on region.
[06:59] Riley Okoye: Do you provide network peering or require VPC peering? We need private connectivity due to PCI/PII constraints.
[07:07] Luis Ortega: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink-like setups. For on-prem we have an appliance option. We'll share network diagrams.

[07:32] Dr. Anika Patel: SOC 2  do you have an up-to-date Type II report?
[07:36] Maya Chen: Yes we do. We'll include our latest SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation in the security pack.

[07:51] Jordan Price: Timeline to procurement approval  if we get the final MSA and pricing today, procurement aims to approve by next Tuesday but Legal/InfoSec may need until Thursday. Is that workable?
[08:02] Maya Chen: That's tight but we can try. We'll send the redlined MSA and the security pack within 24h.

[08:20] Samir Gupta: One clause on indemnity  we want broader IP indemnities. Your standard limits apply. Can we get examples of prior customer language?
[08:30] Maya Chen: We can share precedent language. For enterprise deals we often do carve-outs or mutual indemnities  we'll propose language to close the gap.

[09:02] Riley Okoye: About logging: we need request-level tracing and per-token cost logs sent to Splunk. Is that available?
[09:10] Luis Ortega: We expose detailed logs and cost breakdowns; we can stream logs to your SIEM with structured events. We'll include log schema and sample events.

[09:45] Dr. Anika Patel: SLA measurement  how are outages measured? Is it per-route or per-region?
[09:52] Luis Ortega: Uptime is measured per-route (per endpoint) and aggregated per-region for Dedicated. We'll attach SLA measurement methodology in the appendix.

[10:20] Jordan Price: On the DPA, subprocessor list  we need transparency and 30-day notice for new subprocessors.
[10:28] Maya Chen: We maintain a subprocessors list and provide notice for changes. We can commit to 30-day notification for material changes.

[10:55] Samir Gupta: For data deletion certification, we'd like an affidavit or signed confirmation from Redwood on completion.
[11:02] Maya Chen: We can provide a certified deletion report signed by our compliance team for hosted customers.

[11:30] Riley Okoye: Performance benchmarks  can you run a short p95 latency test on our representative prompt set? We'd like throughput and cost estimates.
[11:38] Luis Ortega: Yes  we'll run benchmarks in our staging environment against the models you specified. Can you send the prompt corpus and expected concurrency?
[11:46] Jordan Price: We'll share a 200-sample prompt set and target concurrency 50 rps.

[12:10] Maya Chen: OK moving to next steps recap. we'll do the following  Maya to send redlined MSA + DPA and security pack within 24h; Luis to run bench with Riley's prompt set and share results in 5 business days; Maya to include pricing deck and committed spend model; Legal/Procurement to review and aim to return comments by next week.
[12:30] Samir Gupta: Correct. Also please note we need the SOC 2 and pen-test reports before sign.
[12:38] Maya Chen: Will include.

[12:55] Dr. Anika Patel: About the 24h breach notification  we'll need to see if Redwood security can bridge to 48. Please escalate.
[13:04] Maya Chen: Will do, I'll flag to our CISO.

[13:22] Jordan Price: Any blockers on Redwood side for signing next week if we accept the commercial terms?
[13:28] Maya Chen: Main blockers are legal alignment on liability cap and breach notice. We'll try to surface conservative alternatives to help procurement.

[13:45] Riley Okoye: For networking diagrams and runbook, please share the VPC peering steps and KMS rotation doc.
[13:52] Luis Ortega: Yes, will share diagrams and a rotation runbook.

[14:10] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents and schedule a technical checkpoint mid-next-week.
[14:18] Jordan Price: Thanks all.

[14:55] End of meeting. (approx)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "envelope keys" transcribed as "envelope keeps"), filler words, and slight speaker attribution noise.
action_items: Maya Chen - Send redlined MSA and DPA with proposed compromise language on liability and breach notice - Due: 2026-03-05
Maya Chen - Share security pack (SOC 2 Type II, pen test, subprocessors list) and pricing deck - Due: 2026-03-05
Luis Ortega - Run p50/p95 latency and throughput benchmarks against Stellar prompt set (50 rps) and share results - Due: 2026-03-11
Riley Okoye - Provide 200-sample prompt corpus and expected concurrency details - Due: 2026-03-05
Samir Gupta - Return legal comments on MSA redlines after internal review - Due: 2026-03-12
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA and security pack within 24 hours
Customer to review documents with Legal/InfoSec and provide consolidated feedback
SE to run performance benchmarks and share cost/latency estimates
